question: Let \(f\) be a function for which \(f\!\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) = x^2 + x + 1.\) Find the sum of all values of \(z\) for which \(f(3z) = 7.\)
solution:
To use the given rule for \(f(3z)\), its input \(x/3\) must equal \(3z\). Thus \(x=9z\), or \(z=x/9\). It is simpler to find the corresponding values of \(x\) first.

The given output equals \(7\) exactly when
\[
x^2+x+1=7,
\]
which is equivalent to
\[
x^2+x-6=(x+3)(x-2)=0.
\]
A product is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero, so the only possibilities are \(x=-3\) and \(x=2\). Therefore
\[
z=-\frac13\quad\text{or}\quad z=\frac29.
\]
Each value corresponds to a root of the original output equation, and the relation \(x=9z\) is reversible, so these are all the solutions. Their sum is
\[
-\frac13+\frac29=\boxed{-\frac19},
\]
choice B.
